question: Who took charge as the Director General of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) in September 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrit Mohan Prasad**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Amrit Mohan Prasad** was appointed as the **Director General** of the **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** in **September 2024**. 
• The **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** is one of the **Central Armed Police Forces** (CAPF) of India, responsible for guarding the borders of India with **Nepal** and **Bhutan**. 
• Amrit Mohan Prasad is a distinguished officer with extensive experience in the field of law enforcement and border security. 
• He succeeds the outgoing Director General and has been tasked with ensuring the **effective functioning of the SSB** and maintaining the security of India’s borders. 
• The appointment of the Director General of SSB is a significant decision as it directly impacts the operational efficiency and strategic planning of India’s border security system. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB):** 
• The **SSB** was established in **1963** in the wake of the **Chinese aggression** and was initially tasked with fostering a sense of security among the people living in border areas. 
• It operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, Government of India. 
• The SSB’s primary duties include **border guarding**, **counter-insurgency operations**, and **providing assistance during natural disasters**. 
• **Role of the Director General:** 
• The Director General (DG) is the **highest-ranking official** in the SSB and oversees all operations, planning, and administration. 
• The DG is responsible for implementing government policies and ensuring the operational preparedness of the force. 
• **Other Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF):** 
• In addition to the SSB, India has several other CAPFs, including the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**, **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)**, and **Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)**. 
• Each of these forces is tasked with specific responsibilities, ranging from border security to industrial safety and counter-terrorism. 
• **Key Challenges Faced by SSB:** 
• Securing borders with **porous boundaries** shared with Nepal and Bhutan. 
• Combating **illegal immigration**, **smuggling**, and **human trafficking** across the borders. 
• Maintaining peace and order in sensitive border regions and fostering **community development programs**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The Director General of SSB is generally appointed from the **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, ensuring that the officer has extensive knowledge and experience in law enforcement and border management. 
• The SSB also plays a vital role in **humanitarian efforts** during natural disasters and emergencies in border regions. 
• India’s **border security strategy** is continuously evolving, with a focus on adopting modern technology and improving infrastructure in border areas. 
• Effective leadership in the SSB is crucial to maintaining the **integrity of India’s borders** and ensuring the safety of border communities.
